sentences.text:
Date : 08.11.2024 Heard Mr. P.R. Sarma, learned counsel for the petitioners; Ms. R. Borah, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL for the respondent nos. 1, 2 & 3; Ms. G. Hazarika, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue & Disaster Management Department for the respondent no. 4; and Mr. S. Baruah,
learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam for the respondent nos. 5, 6 & 7.
Page No.# 5/7 2.

The petitioners, 11 [eleven] in nos., have projected that they are in possession of different parcels of land, covered by Dag nos. 145, 203, 369, at Village - Tarapara, Dudhnoi Revenue Circle, District Goalpara since about 20 to 30 years and have constructed structures thereon in order to earn their livelihoods.

3. A process of land acquisition under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 has been undertaken and in the process of acquisition which has been undertaken for the purpose of a project named '4-laning from Paikan to Dhupdhara [PKG-8]' in District - Goalpara, the Additional Deputy Page No.# 1/7 vs The Union Of India And 6 Ors on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157434819/
4
Commissioner, Goalpara is the Competent Authority Land Acquisition [CALA] under Section 3[a] of the National Highways Act, 1956.

It transpires from a Letter dated 05.11.2024 [Annexure-5], written to the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Goalpara and the Circle Officer, Dudhnoi Revenue Circle,
Goalpara that notices had been served to the awardees/interested persons/possessors and certain portion of compensation for zirat, structures, had been paid.

But, it has been reported by the Requiring Authority, M/s NHIDCL that there have been hindrance within the Right of Way [RoW]
and the same have caused delay in the construction works of the National Highway.

The said authorities have been requested for clearing the acquired lands who had already received notices and to evict the structures within the RoW in coordination with the Superintendent of Police,
Goalpara and the concerned NHIDCL authorities ensuring photographic and videographic evidence regarding the eviction drives.
4.

Mr. Sarma, learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that today some of the petitioners have been served with a notice under sub-section [2] of the Section 26 of the Control of National Highways [Land and Traffic] Act, 2002, providing them 4 [four] days time to remove the structures which they claimed to be unauthorized in the Right of Way [RoW] of the National Highway.

entities.text: Control of National Highways [Land and Traffic] Act, 2002
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. Ms. Borah, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL has submitted that from the Letter dated 05.11.2024, it is evident that the land has been acquired after due issuance of Notifications under Section 3A and Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956.

As such, the acquired land has vested absolutely in the Central Government free from all Page No.# 6/7 encumbrances and as a result, the Right of Way [RoW] belongs to the respondent authorities, more particularly, the Central Government.

As per the provisions contained in Section 3E of the National Highways Act, 1956,
where any land has vested in the Central Government under Section 3D, the petitioners should vacate from the place by removing the structures.

Ms. Borah has drawn attention to the applications submitted by the petitioners and the contents of the writ petition to submit that the structures constructed by the petitioners have already been marked during the survey conducted during the process of acquisition.

6. Issue notice, returnable on 06.12.2024.
7.

As Ms. Borah, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDC has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent nos. 1, 2 & 3; Ms. Hazarika, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue & Disaster Management Department has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent no. 4; and Mr. Baruah, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent nos. 5, 6 & 7, issuance of formal notice to the said respondents, stands dispensed with.
However, extra copy of the writ petition along with annexures is to be furnished to Ms. Borah, Ms. Hazarika and Mr. Baruah within 3 [three] working days from today.
8. Mr. Sarma, learned counsel for the petitioners has prayed for an interim relief.

9. Having regard to the fact that the stage of the proceedings under Section 3A and Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956 are already over and the land has vested absolutely in the Central Government in view of the provisions contained a sub-section [2] of Section 3D of the National Page No.# 1/7 vs The Union Of India And 6 Ors on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157434819/
5 Highways Act, 1956, this Court is not persuaded to pass any order stalling the process initiated by the respondent authorities.

If the petitioners have been served with notices under sub-section [2] of Section 26 of the Control of National Highways [Land & Traffic] Act, 2002, the petitioners are at liberty to approach the appropriate authorities in terms of the provisions contained in Section 26 of the Control of National Highways [Land & Traffic] Act, 2002 by submitting representations within a period of 4 [four] days as mentioned in the said notice, as contended by Mr. Sarma, learned counsel for the Page No.# 7/7 petitioners.
